artists.biography:
Matthew Charles "Matt" Berry (born 2 May 1974) is an English actor, writer, comedian and musician. Berry is perhaps best known for his appearances in The IT Crowd, Garth Marenghi's Darkplace, The Mighty Boosh, and Snuff Box. He is renowned for his deep voice; he has voiced several advertisements, most notably for Volvic, The Natural Confectionery Company, Absolute Radio, and MoneySupermarket.

As a musician, Berry composed all the music for Snuff Box, as well as the music for AD/BC: A Rock Opera, which he co-wrote with Richard Ayoade. AD/BC was a half-hour parody of overblown musicals in general and Jesus Christ Superstar in particular, telling the story of the innkeeper who allowed Mary, Joseph, and the baby Jesus to sleep in his manger. AD/BC was broadcast in December 2004 and featured Fulcher and Mighty Boosh stars Julian Barratt and Noel Fielding. He also performed a song for an episode of Garth Marenghi's Darkplace entitled "One Track Lover", a spoof of cheesy romantic 80s songs.

perplexity.description:
Heard Noises is the eleventh studio album by English musician Matt Berry, released on January 24, 2025, via Acid Jazz Records, marking his return to vocal-driven material after the 2023 instrumental Simplicity and the 2021 album The Blue Elephant. Blending '70s prog structures with '60s pop sensibilities, the record showcases Berry's multi-instrumental prowess—he plays nearly every instrument, including acoustic and electric guitars, various keyboards like ARP synthesizer, Farfisa organ, Mellotron, Minimoog, Hammond B3, and Wurlitzer piano, as well as glockenspiel and xylophone—while handling production, mixing, engineering, and even cover art. Collaborators such as drummer Craig Blundell, alongside guests like Natasha Lyonne, Eric D. Johnson, Phil Scragg, and Kitty Durham from Kitty, Daisy & Lewis, add depth to its groovy psych-pop sound rooted in rock influences.

Spanning 14 tracks like "Why On Fire?," "Silver Rings," "Be Alarmed," "Wedding Photo Stranger," "Stay On The Ground," "There Are Monsters," "Canada Dry," "The Snakes Will Slide," and "Sky High," with brief interludes enhancing its seamless flow, the album delivers vibrant, rewritten psychedelic history that plays cohesively from start to finish. Critics hailed it as a standout in Berry's discography: AllMusic placed it "right near the top," potentially at the summit; BrooklynVegan dubbed it "another groovy psych-pop gem" and "A Matt Berry Primer"; and tmrw praised its structural fusion and listenability. Metacritic aggregated a score of 84/100 from five reviews, signifying universal acclaim.

The album's reception underscores Berry's songwriting and production mastery, available in formats like marbled serenity blue vinyl (Rough Trade exclusive, limited to 500), standard blue and black vinyl, CD, cassette, and a signed box set edition, cementing its place as a soulful, genre-spanning triumph in his eighth outing with Acid Jazz.
